Work consists of analyzing data, researching extensively, delivering results, creating interactive dashboards, and ensuring data quality. The position supports all Community Services programs and initiatives division-wide. Serves as a subject matter expert in data analysis, data quality, reporting, and performance measurements. Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) Community Services’ division seeks a highly qualified candidate to fill the Data Analyst IV position within Business Operations. The ideal candidate excels in teamwork, upholds high standards and accountability, embraces curiosity and learning, applies critical thinking to tasks, and uses creativity for innovation. Reporting to the Manager of Data and System Operations, the Data Analyst IV handles advanced data analysis and research tasks. Work consists of analyzing data, researching extensively, delivering results, creating interactive dashboards, and ensuring data quality. The position supports all Community Services programs and initiatives division-wide. Serves as a subject matter expert in data analysis, data quality, reporting, and performance measurements. Analyzes content, structure, and relationships within data to identify trends, patterns, gaps, inconsistencies, and opportunities for improvement. Works closely with program stakeholders to understand business requirements, develops reporting solutions, and supports data-driven decision making. Provides recommendations regarding systematic changes that improve data collection processes and aligns data infrastructure with business needs. May mentor staff and provide technical guidance related to reporting, analytics, and data visualization initiatives.

Additional responsibilities include reporting activities for the division through the preparation and analysis of a variety of data. Responsible for accurate reporting, along with the development of a variety of reporting outputs to meet the needs of multiple internal and external stakeholders. Analyzes divisional program and financial data to reveal trends and drive strategy. Identifies data gaps, errors, anomalies, inconsistencies, and redundancies in data sources and reporting processes. Adhoc assignments related to program areas, special assignments and other duties as assigned. Brief Job Description

Come work in an environment where we truly value and respect those we serve and believe in the mission that all people can achieve a higher level of wellness and independence.

The state supported living centers serve people with intellectual and developmental disabilities who are medically fragile or who have behavioral problems. The centers provide campus-based direct services and supports at 13 centers located throughout the state. Learn About Our State Supported Living Centers

If you are looking for a place to work where you can establish a career that is filled with purpose, this is the job for you!

Driver’s License is required

The Direct Support Professional (DSP) IV: Residential Scheduler/Mealtime Program Coordinator reports to the Director of Residential Services (DRS). The DSP IV: Residential Scheduler/MTC Program Coordinator works closely with the DRS to ensure the Mealtime Coordination Process is followed, which includes the training, observation, data collection and review, and presentation of the Mealtime Coordination process. Works closely with the DRS to ensure residential master schedules are complete, accurate, and coverage of each home is met. The DSP IV Residential Scheduler/MTC Program Coordinator is responsible for the oversight of all training activities to ensure staff are appropriately oriented and trained. May serve as a liaison between the training department and residential units. Works under limited supervision with considerable latitude for the use of initiative and independent judgment.

This position is required to drive a state-owned vehicle.

Essential Job Functions (EJFs)

Attends work on a regular basis and may be required to work a specific shift schedule or, at times, even a rotating schedule, extended shift and/or overtime in accordance with agency leave policy and performs other duties as assigned.

Arranges and provides oversight work schedules to ensure adequate coverage and staff/individual ratios are appropriate.

Attends meetings, serves on committee, and performs other specific tasks when directed by the Director of Residential Services, ADoP, or facility Director.

Ensure residential staff are current with facility and agency core and specialty competency-based training, which includes orientation, refresher, and local training requirements.

Ensures residential staff complete post-orientation (on-the-job) training in the residential setting, when needed, and completes required documentation.

Maintains residential employee training letters.

Conduct competency-based training of staff; monitoring programs; monitoring availability, condition, and proper use of assistive equipment; and ensuring appropriate availability and condition of PNMP instructions and illustrations during mealtimes

Provide new employee orientation and refresher training as indicated and will provide direct training of new employees with specific individuals served in mealtime procedures

Ensure that the dining room is maintained as a safe and sanitary environment for individuals in the unit

Monitors meals and snacks to ensure safe eating practices.

Reviews data, conducts audits and inter-rater, and analyzes data by utilizing the SSLC Monitoring and Tracking System (MATS) for presentation of the mealtime program to QA/QI Committee.

Plans, assigns and supervises work of others during mealtime of the homes

Other duties as assigned include but are not limited to actively participating and/or serving in a supporting role to meet the agency’s obligations for disaster response and/or recovery or Continuity of Operations (COOP) activation. Such participation may require an alternate shift pattern assignment and/or location.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities (KSAs)

Ability to organize schedules.
Skills in staff scheduling and deployment at a residential facility.
Knowledge of mealtime process.
Ability to counsel and train others.
Ability to evaluate and communicate to staff.
Ability to interact effectively with individuals and staff.
Ability to work with various teams.
Ability to interpret regulations, policies, and procedures.
Skill in professional oral and written communication.
Ability to perform basic and complex math calculations.
Skills in using computers and agency/facility software including, but not limited to, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Access, Outlook, and SharePoint.
Able to generate data by graphing/charting and providing an analysis of data.
Ability to communicate verbally and in writing in a clear and concise manner.

Registrations, Licensure Requirements Or Certifications

Valid Texas driver’s license or ability to obtain it no later than 90 days after hire date, is required. Applicants with an out-of-state driver’s license must provide an original certified driving record from the state of driving licensure. Eligible driving record required based on HHSC Fleet Management policy.

Initial Screening Criteria

High school diploma or GED is preferred.

Two (2) years’ experience working in the field related to this position (working with people with developmental or physical disabilities).

Additional Information

Applicants must pass a fingerprint criminal background check, pre-employment drug screen, and registry checks including the Client Abuse/Neglect Reporting System (CANRS), Nurse Aide, Medication Aide and Employee Misconduct and HHS List of Excluded Individuals/ Entities (LEIE).

Males between the ages of 18 – 25 must be registered with the Selective Service.

All State Supported Living Center Employees are subject to Random Drug Testing.

Flexibility in work hours may be required for this position. The position may be required to work overtime and/or extended hours. Must be willing to work weekends and holidays.

About Romix 
Romix Biosciences is a biotechnology company developing a cell-free RNA platform that reveals what is happening inside the body without a biopsy. Our programs span multiple disease settings with leading medical centers and biopharma partners across the country.

About the Job
We are looking for a Research Program Coordinator to own the operational backbone of our translational research projects and to keep the company running smoothly day to day.  The ideal candidate is an excellent communicator, is detail-oriented, and can operate independently. This job offers direct exposure to many aspects of biomedical innovation and direct interfacing with world leading researchers. It is an excellent opportunity to own a process outright at a fast growing biotech startup.

As a member of our team you will:
Serve as a coordinator for multiple collaborative projects funded by NIH SBIR/STTR awards, nonprofit foundations, and biopharma partnerships
Manage relationships with research partners, including meetings, IRB submissions, and biospecimen logistics
Manage administrative responsibilities for the executive team
Track budgets and support financial reporting to NIH program officers and finance team
Coordinate lab purchasing and monitor reagent and consumable inventories
Have the opportunity to grow with the company into adjacent areas such business development, grant writing, or lab operations

Qualifications
Required

Bachelor's or Master’s degree
Strong organizational judgment and the ability to prioritize independently in an environment with competing deadlines
Proficiency with Google Workspace, Slack, and Notion, and the ability to pick up new systems quickly
1+ years of experience in a research, healthcare, or operations setting
Ability to build agentic coworkers for routine tasks

Preferred

Exposure to IRB submissions and/or research agreements such as MTAs, DUAs, and CDAs move through an institution
Experience supporting NIH-funded research, including SBIR/STTR mechanisms, subawards, or progress reporting
Experience handling human biospecimens and working knowledge of shipping regulations for biological materials (IATA, Category B)
Experience with LIMS, electronic lab notebooks, or clinical data capture systems
Prior experience at a startup or in a small team working independently

Why Join Us
Own a key process end-to-end, with real influence over how it is built
Work directly with the founding team and with researchers from leading medical centers
See your work change how patients are treated
Monthly health insurance stipend (QSHERA) and flexible time off
Broad exposure to how a company is built, how large contracts are executed, and how medicine is innovated
